basis: Prepare one complete proposed drawer-handle geometry basis for the declared review. The connected original prompt, scaled reference, context and user profile are authoritative inputs. Preserve X drawer width, Y vertical, Z outward and mounting plane Z=0; mounting centers (0,0) and (96,0), flat 18 by 24 by 5 mm pads, 4.5 mm through holes and supplied M4 hardware without plastic threads. Preserve the label keepout below Y=-18, outer envelope at most 118 by 28 by 34 mm, at least 25 mm finger clearance behind the central 65 mm grip, nominal 12 by 9 mm oval grip, internal blends at least 3 mm where space permits, touched rounds at least 1 mm, and 1.5 mm thumb recess over the central 40 mm. Resolve smooth arch construction and all predictable numeric design choices in this proposed basis. Retain P1S 0.4 mm PETG, 0.20 mm layers, five walls and 40% infill. Record 40 N drawer-opening intent, ambient 10–40 C and wipe cleaning as design inputs, not verified performance. The item is a prototype, not a lifting/load-restraint handle. No physical fit, load, fatigue, food, dishwasher, print or certification claim. Compare pads-down and side using later actual packages/support paths; a geometry-only preview and exact dimension review precede every slice. Do not ask unattended questions. Return only valid JSON under 5000 characters with scenario_id, supplied_requirements, proposed_geometry, basis_review, remaining_verification and engineering_acceptance=false.
qualified_basis: Retain the connected supplied geometry basis numeric choices exactly. Its scenario_id must match this handle assignment. The basis and configured operation remain proposals pending this run's declared review; they do not establish measured or physical compliance.
basis_review: Review the exact original 96 mm scale, coordinate frame, mounting holes and pads, label keepout, finger clearance, oval grip, thumb recess and edge treatments. Resolve the complete proposed geometry before construction. Preserve the original 10 requirements and all later exact-output checks. This basis decision is not a dimension measurement, load/fit validation or permission for physical operation. The explicit Orca 2.4.2 binding and the only profile mapping (automatic support-wall value -1 to 0) require this accepted source revision. Review the selected final orientation and both declared candidates. Geometry remains in original model coordinates; build orientation is a separate Core3MF instance transform.
configured_review: The connected construction/repair arguments are invoked exactly. Compare those operation templates and their pinned bytes against this handle basis and original requirements before releasing this barrier. Run-resolved calls are separate evidence. A prior operation or labelled digital test decision is not human engineering acceptance.
create: Construct the reviewed drawer handle from the actual supplied reference and original dimensions using the selected geometry capability. The declared basis review releases digital construction only. Keep every mounting, keepout, clearance, grip, recess and envelope requirement; do not substitute a plain bar or claim fit from appearance. Export binary STL in explicit mm to {source_mesh}, with at most 80000 triangles, in the original X/Y/Z model frame. Use uniquely owned objects. For Blender use guarded bpy/bmesh/mathutils and STL export; no raw filesystem, network, process, handler, timer, driver or unrelated-object operations. Preserve the connected original_user_prompt verbatim as user_prompt in each execute_blender_code call. Return compact actual observations and explicit technical failure if the reviewed geometry cannot be produced. No new unattended question or invented evidence.
configured_construction: Submit the connected qualified_operation code unchanged to execute_blender_code, preserving the original user prompt in user_prompt. Check it against reviewed_basis; a mismatch blocks execution. The pinned operation is a proposed recipe and does not establish actual compliance.
repair: Import the actual source STL {source_mesh}; preserve its bytes and original X drawer-width/Y vertical/Z outward frame. Inspect actual bounds, manifold topology, degeneracy, normals and all handle features. Repair only with recorded small mm tolerances, preserving dimensions, holes, pads, clearance, label keepout and touched surfaces. Export distinct binary STL {repaired_mesh}, at most 80000 triangles. Do not rotate this acceptance subject into a build frame: downstream comparison derives pads-down and side from these exact repaired bytes. Retain real geometry-only preview {mesh_preview}; it is not a support/toolpath preview. Use guarded bpy/bmesh/mathutils, STL import/export and render with uniquely owned objects and no raw filesystem/network/process APIs. Preserve original_user_prompt verbatim in each execute_blender_code user_prompt. Report actual before/after dimensions and all unresolved features. A declared persisted dimension/preview review must complete before any slicer stage. Fail if intended features or closed manifold geometry cannot be preserved.
configured_repair: Submit the connected qualified_operation code unchanged to execute_blender_code. It must preserve the original model frame and consume this run's actual source. Retain real measurements, repair/export completion and geometry preview; partial output or provider error cannot establish success.
geometry_review: Inspect this run's exact repaired mesh, geometry-only preview and construction/repair records BEFORE ANY SLICING. Review the mounting centers/4.5 mm holes/flat pads, label keepout, 118 by 28 by 34 mm envelope in original model axes, 25 mm clearance over central 65 mm, 12 by 9 mm grip, rounds/blends and thumb recess against original files and requirements. Record any missing dimensions or visual evidence and request correction instead of accepting incomplete evidence. This durable local review releases digital preparation only, not physical fit/strength/printing acceptance. Later support/orientation review remains mandatory.
report: Read the supplied original requirements and construction/repair records directly. Read the connected slice_evidence, toolpath_summary and orientation_comparison JSON reference contents supplied with their exact paths and hashes. Each reference has a 32768-byte inline limit; if only identity metadata is supplied or any required observation is absent, report that limitation and keep the corresponding requirement unresolved. Do not guess unread contents, call tools, read raw profiles/G-code/full previews or write another file. Wright saves this response. Summarize exact handle geometry and preparation evidence, five walls/40% infill PETG settings, original model frame and unresolved support-contact review. Summarize the supplied orientation comparison while retaining both exact support views for the declared final manual review; the comparison does not establish actual support-contact acceptance and unread view contents must not be inferred from filenames or geometry. Separate measured dimensions from design proposals and physical claims. The connected slice evidence names the explicitly selected final orientation. Its package derives from the unchanged repaired STL through the declared standard 3MF build transform. Report all three exact hashes and the actual native engine/settings. The other candidate supplies comparison only; a choice change requires an accepted source revision and fresh exact downstream bindings. Return one JSON object under 6000 characters with artifact_lineage, geometry_observations, preparation_observations, outstanding_requirements, limitations and engineering_acceptance=false.
final_review: Review every original Printed02 requirement against exact outputs: mounting centers/holes/pads, label keepout, clearance, oval grip/recess/rounds, envelope in original model axes, original/repaired lineage, both prepared Core3MF build matrices and actual Orca packages, classified support views, support-contact locations and removability, exact PETG five-wall/40% profiles, actual effective settings and native result, simulated receipt and action scope. The explicit engine binding names the final orientation; its original repaired STL, prepared 3MF and native package digests must all correspond. The other orientation is comparison evidence. Review nominal paths in their declared G-code frame with the retained effective extruder offset and inverse model transform; do not mistake their raw coordinates for original mounting coordinates. Unknown paths and required feature/contact evidence stay explicit. Reject unresolved requirements instead of inferring compliance from a preview. This digital result does not establish physical fit, 40 N load, fatigue, printing, lifting suitability or certification. Changing selection is a visible source correction, invalidating affected preparation, package, review and receipt subjects.
orientation_basis: Compare pads-down and side from the same unchanged repaired binary STL in original model axes. Preserve all original 10 requirements and 18 checks. Prepare Core3MF with original mesh coordinates and a proper rigid build transform, centered at 128,128 mm on bed Z=0. Pads-down uses identity rotation; side uses +90 degrees around X. Slice each actual prepared package once with the declared independent shell MCP and Orca 2.4.2 engine. Preserve source/prepared/native hashes, both packages, actual native results/effective profiles and exact nominal support views. Independent oriented-triangle correspondence and inverse model reconstruction allow at most 0.0001 mm serialization error, inherited from the original orientation conversion bound to accommodate float32 recentering; this is not an engineering dimension tolerance. Original model-axis envelope and feature requirements are unchanged. Retain unknown path classifications; counts and lengths are not contact/removability simulation. Compare contact around mounting pads/holes, finger opening, touched surfaces and thumb recess at final review. The typed selected_orientation controls final package binding in this revision. Other candidate evidence neither selects nor approves itself. Changes require explicit revised source and downstream invalidation; no physical machine action or automatic engineering acceptance.
